sense: of a play, a film or a show

terms.gloss: the producer, who supplies what a show needs
evidence: Plaut. Pers. 1.3.79, Trin. 4.2.16, Curc. 4.1 (old numbering; Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From Greek χορηγός, the citizen who paid for a chorus. In Plautus he is the man who hires out the costumes and props for a play, and in the Curculiō he steps on stage himself to fret about his costumes (Lewis & Short); Traupman gives the word for a producer. Lewis & Short also cites it, once, for the one who pays for a banquet (Suet. Aug. 70).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 169, 365 (producer).
